target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter second-collection insertion (sub_08011732)
target.role: append a migrated element to the second collection
target.notes: sub_08011732, 216 bytes and 97 instructions, one terminator at 0x08011808. THE INSERTION IS AT 0x0801177E..0x0801178A and reads `slot = second.count; second.count = slot + 1; second.elements[slot] = element`, using the OLD count as the index. HOW IT IS REACHED: the routine walks the FIRST collection BACKWARD from count-1 to 0 and asks each element's virtual method at table+0x18, passing a pass counter. A verdict of 1 makes it call table+0x04 and REMOVE the element from the first collection. A verdict of 2 makes it call table+0x1C, APPEND the element to the SECOND collection and REMOVE it from the first. Any other verdict leaves the element alone. So the second collection is filled by a VERDICT-DRIVEN MIGRATION out of the first, and the element is MOVED rather than copied: it exists in exactly one of the two collections afterwards. THE SECOND COLLECTION IS REACHED BY A COMPUTED BASE: the 0x40C literal is loaded into a register and added, so a displacement search finds nothing, exactly as in sub_080119BC. THIS IS THE INVERSE OF sub_080119BC, which moves an element from the second collection to the first when a key is found; together they are the two directions of one migration. ORDER: the inner loop runs BACKWARD, the same direction as the reader sub_08011C70 and the opposite of sub_080119BC's forward keyed scan. NO DUPLICATE CHECK: the element is appended at the tail whether or not an equal element is already in the second collection, so duplicate prevention is NOT a property of this path. NO CAPACITY CHECK and no bounds check on the second count. A THIRD COLLECTION EXISTS AT object + 0x208: the routine walks it calling table+0x14 on each element and then SETS ITS COUNT TO ZERO, so that collection is FLUSHED rather than migrated. THE REMOVAL HELPER TAKES THE COUNT SLOT, NOT THE COLLECTION BASE, which this routine proves by passing object + 4 for the first collection; the same convention means the call in sub_080119BC is sub_0804FE54(object + 0x40C, index) and an earlier note of ours saying object + 0x408 is corrected here. +0x00 IS NOT TOUCHED. UNKNOWN: what the elements are, what verdicts 1 and 2 mean beyond their effect, what sub_080116FC/sub_080115B0/sub_0803DA62 and the global at 0x08072824 do, and what appends to the third collection. No semantic name is assigned and nothing is imported from another title.
